judged_text: createEvent now selects the target calendar only via destinationCalendar.find(cal => cal.credentialId === credentialId) and silently falls back to "primary" when no entry matches, discarding destination externalIds whose entries lack a credentialId. For bookings whose destinationCalendar has no credentialId — the legacy path EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents explicitly still serves by calling createEvent for every same-integration credential — the Google event is created on each credential's "primary" calendar instead of the configured destination calendar; a user with two Google credentials gets duplicate events on both primaries where the old code created exactly one event on the destination (the non-owner's 404 was swallowed).

For bookings whose destinationCalendar has no credentialId — the legacy path EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents explicitly still serves by calling createEvent for every same-integration credential — the Google event is created on each credential's "primary" calendar instead of the configured destination calendar; a user with two Google credentials gets duplicate events on both primaries where the old code created exactly one event on the destination (the non-owner's 404 was swallowed).

adjudication.rationale: In `GoogleCalendarService.createEvent`, the target calendar is now chosen only via `calEventRaw.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.credentialId === credentialId)?.externalId`, and `calendarId` falls back to `"primary"` when no match is found (insert uses `selectedCalendar || "primary"`). Since `destinationCalendar` is now an array and entries can lack `credentialId` (see `EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents`: else-branch for destinations without `credentialId` calls `createEvent(c, event)` for every same-integration credential), Google events for those legacy/no-credentialId destinations will be created on each credential’s primary calendar rather than the configured `externalId`. The optional `externalId` passed through `CalendarManager.createEvent(..., externalId?)` is not used to select the calendar in the Google service, so it doesn’t prevent this. This is a behavior regression and can lead to duplicate events across multiple Google credentials’ primaries compared to the previous single-`externalId` behavior.
